Configuration

Complete reference for ~/.config/mailypoppins/config.toml

Config File Location

All configuration lives in a single file: ~/.config/mailypoppins/config.toml. Create it interactively with mp config init, or write it by hand. View the resolved config at any time with mp config show. Print the file path with mp config path.

A key mailypoppins does not know, such as a typo like sync_intervall_secs, does not stop the file from loading: it is ignored, and mp prints a warning naming it and its account on every command, as do the daemon log, mp daemon health, the TUI's activity log and a banner line in the desktop app.

Full Example

A complete single-account configuration with comments explaining each section.

theme = "mailypoppins"  # TUI color theme (see Theme section)
notifications = false       # TUI notifications for new mail and reminders (see Notifications section)

[email]
font_family = "Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"  # HTML email font
font_size = "16px"                             # HTML email font size
include_signature = true                       # Append signature to outgoing mail
send_hold_secs = 20                            # Undo-send window before hand-off (0 = send now)

[smtp]
host = "postout.lrz.de"
port = 587
username = "your-id"
default_from = "your.name@example.com"
# Password stored in the secrets store, not here

[imap]
host = "imap.example.com"   # Falls back to smtp.host if omitted
port = 993
username = ""               # Falls back to smtp.username if omitted
fetch_concurrency = 4       # Mailboxes fetched in parallel per sync (1-8)
body_fetch_deadline_secs = 30  # Per-mailbox download budget on a TUI sync (0 = unbounded)
sync_interval_secs = 900    # Daemon syncs after this long without a sync (0 = never)
# Password falls back to SMTP password if not set separately

# Every server folder is found without an entry here; these pin and override.
[mailboxes.inbox]
server = "INBOX"            # IMAP folder name; its messages are stored
                            # under the key "inbox" in the account database

[mailboxes.archive]
server = "Archive"

[mailboxes.sent]
server = "Sent Items"

[[mailboxes.extra]]         # A folder always synced, whatever discovery decides
server = "Projects"

[[mailboxes.override]]      # Change the policy of the folders a glob matches
match = "Labels/*"
policy = "ignore"           # sync | status-only | ignore

The file has no signature keys: each signature is a Markdown file under ~/.config/mailypoppins/signatures/. See Signatures.

Section Breakdown

theme

Selects the TUI color theme by name (helix-style: themes are built in and picked in config, not defined in separate files). The key is top-level, so it must appear before the first [section] header. Available themes:

  • mailypoppins: the default, used when the key is omitted; the Mac app's dark palette (aliases: mailypoppins-dark, default)
  • mailypoppins-light: the Mac app's light palette
  • catppuccin-mocha: the TUI's original look (alias: catppuccin)
  • catppuccin-latte: its light variant (alias: latte)
  • tokyo-night (alias: tokyonight)
  • terminal: adapts to the terminal's own ANSI palette: the background shows through and colors follow your terminal theme (aliases: transparent, ansi)

Names are case-insensitive. An unknown name does not fail: the TUI starts with the default theme and logs a warning to the activity log.

Every theme except terminal paints its own background, so the TUI draws a rounded frame around the whole screen in the theme's border colour to mark where it ends and your terminal begins. terminal has no edge to mark and uses the full window. 

theme = "catppuccin-mocha"

notifications

Opt-in desktop notifications for new mail while the TUI is running (default: false). Like theme, the key is top-level, so it must appear before the first [section] header. When a background sync (including the automatic IDLE-triggered fetches) saves new emails to the inbox, one notification is shown per sync: sender: subject for a single new email, or N new emails when several arrive at once. Read-status updates, duplicate cleanup, and mailboxes other than the inbox never trigger a notification.

The same key turns on the TUI's notification of a calendar reminder that fires while no desktop app is open; the desktop app always notifies of reminders, so a TUI and the app open together notify once.

Notifications use the platform's native tooling — osascript on macOS and notify-send on Linux — and degrade silently if the tool is unavailable. 

notifications = true

[email]

Controls the HTML rendering of sent emails. The font family and size are applied to the generated HTML when Markdown is converted for sending. include_signature determines whether the account signature is appended to a draft body on compose, reply, and forward. send_hold_secs is the undo-send window: in the TUI a send is held for that many seconds before it is handed to SMTP, and u cancels it in the meantime, leaving the draft untouched. It defaults to 20 seconds; set it to 0 to send immediately. 

[email]
font_family = "Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"
font_size = "16px"
include_signature = true
send_hold_secs = 20

[smtp]

SMTP settings for sending email. The password is kept in the secrets store under the key smtp-password-<account> (see Password Storage). It is never written to the config file. 

[smtp]
host = "postout.lrz.de"
port = 587
username = "your-id"
default_from = "your.name@example.com"

[imap]

IMAP settings for fetching, syncing, and watching mailboxes. host, port and username fall back to their SMTP counterparts if omitted, so you only need to specify them when the IMAP server differs from SMTP.

fetch_concurrency is how many mailboxes a single sync fetches in parallel, each on its own connection (default 4, clamped to the range 1-8). A sync opens one connection per mailbox and overlaps their latency, so more mailboxes finish in about the time of one. Lower it toward 1 if a server throttles concurrent connections.

body_fetch_deadline_secs is how long a single mailbox may spend downloading message bodies on a sync started by the TUI (default 30, maximum 600, 0 for no limit). A mailbox that runs out of budget stops between batches, keeps what it has downloaded, and resumes on the next sync, so a large backlog arrives over several syncs instead of holding one open; newest mail is downloaded first. Nothing is deleted and no flag delta is advanced on a sync that stopped early. mp sync ignores the budget and always downloads everything it owes.

sync_interval_secs is how long the daemon lets the account go without a sync before it runs a quick one on its own (default 900, fifteen minutes; 0 turns it off; values under 60 are raised to 60). The daemon already syncs when new mail reaches the inbox; this catches what that cannot see, such as changes in other folders, retries of queued changes, and an account with no window open. Any sync, whether you started it or the daemon did, restarts the wait. Microsoft Graph accounts follow the same interval. 

[imap]
host = "imap.example.com"   # Falls back to smtp.host
port = 993
username = ""               # Falls back to smtp.username
fetch_concurrency = 4       # Parallel mailbox fetches per sync (1-8)
body_fetch_deadline_secs = 30  # Per-mailbox body download budget, seconds (0 = unbounded)
sync_interval_secs = 900    # Seconds without a sync before the daemon runs one (0 = never)

Data directory (not configurable)

Mail, drafts, contacts cache, Graph tokens, and logs all live under a single OS-conventional app data directory:

  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/mailypoppins/
  • Linux (incl. WSL): $XDG_DATA_HOME/mailypoppins/ (default ~/.local/share/mailypoppins/)

Layout under the data directory:

mailypoppins/
  accounts/<name>/store.sqlite3          # synced mail: one row per message
  accounts/<name>/blobs/                 # message bodies and attachments, by hash
  accounts/<name>/drafts/                # your drafts, one .md file each
  accounts/<name>/attachments/<msg-id>/  # attachments a forward carries into a draft
  accounts/<name>/contacts-cache.json    # contacts index
  tokens/<name>.enc                      # Graph tokens
  state.json                             # app state: each account's default signature
  logs/mailypoppins-YYYY-MM-DD.log       # daily logs, 200 MB at most in total

mp config show prints the first three paths for every configured account. Synced mail is not a file tree: a message is a row in store.sqlite3 plus content-addressed blobs, and what you read in the TUI is rendered from those. Drafts are the half that is still files, which is what you would symlink into an Obsidian vault: accounts/<name>/drafts/. The location is not user-configurable per account; override the entire data root with MAILYPOPPINS_DATA_DIR=/some/path for tests or portable installs.

[mailboxes]

The daemon lists every folder on the account's server and keeps each one by a policy. Inbox, Sent, Archive and every folder you created sync on every tick. The trash and junk folders and Proton Mail's label folders are status-only: the sidebar shows the server's counts, and only the newest 50 messages of the trash and junk folders are downloaded, so a message another client moved there keeps a row. Exchange's calendar, contact and task folders, Proton's All Mail and Starred, and folders that only hold other folders are ignored. mp list-mailboxes prints each folder's policy, and the reason when it is ignored. A folder found this way needs no entry here: mp sync --mailbox, mp search --mailbox, the sidebar and the gf picker reach it by name.

Synced mail lives in the account's store. The roles inbox, archive and sent are stored under their role name, which is also the mailbox segment of an mp:// selector; every other folder is stored under its server name. The one directory left under the account's data directory is drafts/.

inbox, archive and sent name the folder holding that role, each with a server field (the IMAP folder name), and always sync. drafts, trash and junk name the folder holding that role when the server marks none. A folder the server marks with a special-use attribute (\Sent, \Trash, ...) or calls by a usual name is found without them.

A [[mailboxes.extra]] entry pins a folder: it syncs on every tick whatever discovery decides, and its key is the server name verbatim, as it always was. A [[mailboxes.override]] entry gives the folders its match glob names another policy; * stands for any run of characters, the hierarchy separator included, the match ignores case, and the first matching entry wins. An override cannot sync a folder that only holds other folders, nor unpin a pinned one.

mp config show lists, under [folders], every folder the server listed at the last sync with the policy it gets, ignored folders included. The setup wizards write the drafts, trash, junk and override entries; they pin no extra folder.

Any other name under [mailboxes], such as a [mailboxes.spesen] table written where a [[mailboxes.extra]] entry was meant, is not a mailbox: the config still loads, the table is ignored, and the warning for it says so. 

[mailboxes.inbox]
server = "INBOX"

[mailboxes.archive]
server = "Archive"

[mailboxes.sent]
server = "Sent Items"

[[mailboxes.extra]]
server = "Projects"

[[mailboxes.override]]
match = "Newsletters*"
policy = "status-only"

Signatures

A signature is one Markdown file in ~/.config/mailypoppins/signatures/. The file name without its extension is the signature's name, so work.md is the signature work and creating a signature is creating a file. The account's default is recorded in the app's own state file (<data_dir>/state.json), so config.toml carries nothing about signatures at all. 

~/.config/mailypoppins/signatures/
  work.md
  work-external.md
  personal.md

Press cs in the TUI to manage them: the list shows every signature with the default starred, Enter sets or clears the default, e opens the selected file in $EDITOR, n creates one, r renames, and d deletes after a confirmation. mp config show prints the directory, the default, and a one-line preview of each file.

HTML in a signature file (a rich signature exported from another mail client) is converted to Markdown when it is read, links kept as [text](url), so the draft you edit and both parts of the sent mail are always Markdown, never raw HTML.

The signature is appended to the draft body when you compose, reply, or forward, so it is visible and editable in the draft rather than added on send. An account with no default signature adds nothing. Use -s <name> to pick a signature or --no-signature to skip it for one draft.

Signatures used to live in config.toml under [accounts.signatures.*], inline as text or as a path. The first run after the upgrade copies those entries out to files and keeps the old default, then prints a notice. The tables are dead after that and can be deleted by hand; mailypoppins never rewrites config.toml.

Two accounts could use the same entry name for different signatures, which the flat directory has no room for, so the second one is copied to <account>-<name>.md and that account's default points there. The same name with the same content stays one file. If an entry cannot be copied, because its name is not a usable file name or its path no longer reads, the notice names it and stops telling you the tables can be deleted: they still hold the only copy.

Drafts on the Server

Every account keeps a copy of each draft in its server Drafts folder, so Outlook, Apple Mail, the Proton app and mp on another machine see the same drafts (how it works). It is on by default; turn it off for an account whose server mangles drafts. Graph accounts are not mirrored yet.

Keep one account's drafts local

[[accounts]]
name = "personal"

[accounts.drafts]
mirror = false

Multi-Account Setup

To manage multiple email accounts, use the [[accounts]] array syntax. Each account has its own smtp, imap, and mailboxes sections nested under it. The account name is used to identify it in commands, password keys, and the data-dir layout (accounts/<name>/).

In the TUI and the desktop app, ga opens a list of the accounts: j/k and Enter, or a digit, switch to one, and Esc cancels.

Two-account example

[email]
font_family = "Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"
font_size = "16px"
include_signature = true

# --- First account ---
[[accounts]]
name = "personal"
default_from = "me@example.com"
auth_method = "password"

[accounts.smtp]
host = "smtp.example.com"
port = 587
username = "me@example.com"

[accounts.imap]
host = "imap.example.com"
port = 993

[accounts.mailboxes.inbox]
server = "INBOX"

[accounts.mailboxes.archive]
server = "Archive"

[accounts.mailboxes.sent]
server = "Sent"

# --- Second account ---
[[accounts]]
name = "work"
default_from = "name@company.com"
auth_method = "graph"

[accounts.oauth2]
client_id = "439d7ebd-7898-4df2-b2d6-88bb61e2597b"  # the mailypoppins app
tenant_id = "common"

[accounts.mailboxes.inbox]
server = "inbox"

[accounts.mailboxes.archive]
server = "archive"

[accounts.mailboxes.sent]
server = "sentitems"

Authentication Methods

Each account has an auth_method field that determines how credentials are handled. Two methods are supported: a password over IMAP and SMTP for every IMAP server, and the Graph API for Microsoft 365.

1. Password (default)

Passwords are kept in the secrets store (see Password Storage) and never written to the config file. Their keys follow the pattern smtp-password-<name> and imap-password-<name>. If the IMAP password is not set, it falls back to the SMTP password.

Set or update passwords with:

mp config set-password smtp --account personal

An on-premises Exchange server, one your organisation runs itself, is a password account like any other IMAP server.

Password auth config

[[accounts]]
name = "personal"
default_from = "me@example.com"
auth_method = "password"  # This is the default; can be omitted

[accounts.smtp]
host = "smtp.example.com"
port = 587
username = "me@example.com"

2. Graph API

For every Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online) account. Uses the Microsoft Graph REST API for all mail operations. No app registration of your own is needed: the client ID of the shared mailypoppins app is built in, and the setup wizard (mp config init or mp config add-account, option 3) uses it when you press Enter at the client ID prompt. The tenant defaults to common, which takes any work, school or personal Microsoft account; you can still enter your tenant ID or domain instead.

The first sign-in asks for consent to the app's delegated permissions (Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, offline_access). Until the mailypoppins publisher is verified with Microsoft, an administrator of your organisation has to approve the app at that first sign-in; personal Microsoft accounts are not affected. An organisation that prefers its own app registration enters its client ID at the prompt instead (see Azure App Registration below).

Graph accounts use well-known folder names (inbox, archive, sentitems) instead of IMAP folder names. SMTP and IMAP sections are not needed. 

mp config oauth2-login --account exchange

Graph API config

[[accounts]]
name = "exchange"
default_from = "name@company.com"
auth_method = "graph"

[accounts.oauth2]
client_id = "439d7ebd-7898-4df2-b2d6-88bb61e2597b"  # the mailypoppins app
tenant_id = "common"          # or your tenant ID or domain

[accounts.mailboxes.inbox]
server = "inbox"              # Graph well-known folder name

[accounts.mailboxes.archive]
server = "archive"

[accounts.mailboxes.sent]
server = "sentitems"          # Not "Sent Items"

Microsoft OAuth2 over IMAP and SMTP (auth_method = "oauth2") is retired. A config that still names it loads, and only that account stays blocked: set auth_method = "graph" for Microsoft 365 and run mp config oauth2-login, or remove the line and set a password for on-premises Exchange.

A Graph account also reads its server calendar, which the calendar views show beside the invitation mails. The account key calendar_backend chooses where an account's calendar comes from, independently of its mail: "graph" is the default of a Graph account and "none" the default of every other account, whose invitations are answered by iMIP reply mails. "ews" and "caldav" are reserved for later releases and read as no calendar for now. Setting calendar_backend = "none" on a Graph account keeps its sign-in to the mail permissions.

A Graph account signed in before the calendar arrived has a token without the calendar permission (Calendars.ReadWrite). Mail keeps working, and every client shows calendar needs a re-login (mp config oauth2-login -A <name>) until you sign in again.

Azure App Registration

A Graph account needs an application registered in Azure Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) only when your organisation wants its own app instead of the mailypoppins app. Here is a condensed setup.

  1. Go to portal.azure.com and navigate to Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations > New registration.
  2. Name the app (e.g., "mailypoppins"), set supported account types to "Accounts in this organizational directory only", and leave the redirect URI blank.
  3. In the app's Authentication settings, scroll to Advanced settings and set "Allow public client flows" to Yes. This enables the device code flow.
  4. Under API permissions, add the delegated Microsoft Graph permissions Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send and offline_access.
  5. If permissions show "Needs admin consent", request your IT administrator to grant consent via the Azure portal.
  6. From the app's Overview page, copy the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID into your config's [accounts.oauth2] section.

Password Storage

Passwords for the password auth method are stored, by default, in an encrypted file at ~/.config/mailypoppins/secrets.enc. Its key is derived from the machine ID and your user ID, so the file opens only on the machine and for the user that wrote it: a backup or a copy on another computer stays unreadable. Graph token caches under tokens/ in the data directory are encrypted the same way. No password prompt or keychain dialog appears at runtime.

Keys follow this naming pattern:

  • smtp-password-<account-name>
  • imap-password-<account-name> (falls back to SMTP password if not set)

To set or update a password:

mp config set-password smtp --account personal

The argument is smtp or imap; without --account the first account is used. The password is entered interactively and never echoed to the terminal.

On a new machine, or after a restore from a backup, the file no longer decrypts. mp config reset-secrets removes it and the Graph token caches, then asks for each account's passwords again.

OS keyring (opt-in)

To keep passwords in the OS keyring instead (macOS Keychain, or Secret Service on Linux, such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet), add this top-level key to config.toml, before the first [section] header: 

secrets_backend = "keyring"

The keyring entries use the service name mailypoppins and the same keys as above. Nothing is migrated: set each password again with mp config set-password after the switch, and run mp daemon restart so a running daemon picks up the new backend. On macOS a build signed with a different identity, which every cargo install produces, asks for keychain access again for every entry.
